intro: You're looking for an accountant you can actually get to, someone local who understands your situation and can sit down with you if needed. Whether you run a small business, work for yourself or have years of paperwork to sort out, finding the right local accountant starts with knowing what you need help with. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK accountant who quotes you directly, so you can compare and decide for yourself.
need_heading: What people searching for a local accountant usually need
need_lead: Most people typing this search want someone nearby who can take the worry out of tax and paperwork.
needs: You've started working for yourself and need to know how to register with HMRC and what records to keep.
You run a small business and want help preparing accounts and filing with Companies House on time.
Your tax affairs have grown complicated and you'd like someone local to talk them through with face to face.
You're unsure whether Making Tax Digital affects you and want practical guidance on keeping digital records.
You'd rather deal with an accountant you can visit in person than one you only ever speak to by phone or email.
context_heading: Understanding who can call themselves an accountant
context: In the UK, the word "accountant" on its own is not a protected title, so anyone can use it. Titles such as Chartered Accountant, Chartered Certified Accountant and Chartered Management Accountant are protected, and members are bound by their professional body's ethics, training and complaints rules. It's worth asking which qualifications and body a local accountant belongs to.

Every practice offering accountancy services must also be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC. You can reasonably ask which body supervises a firm, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance and how complaints are handled. That helps you judge for yourself whether a local accountant is right for you.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say what kind of work you do or what your business does, so the accountant can judge whether they're a good fit.
Explain whether you need help with accounts, tax returns, Making Tax Digital, payroll or general business advice.
Mention whether you're a sole trader, a limited company or a partnership, as this affects what's involved.
Describe how far you are from your nearest town or city, so we can look for someone genuinely local to you.
Say whether you'd prefer to meet in person, work remotely, or a mix of both.
Include anything time-sensitive, such as a filing deadline you're worried about, without needing exact figures.
questions_heading: Questions to ask a local accountant
questions: Which professional body are you a member of, and what qualifications do you hold?
Which body supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance, and how are complaints handled?
Exactly which returns and filings does your quote cover?
How do you handle Making Tax Digital for clients like me?
Can we meet in person locally, and how often would you suggest reviewing my affairs?

faqs.q: Why does it matter that an accountant is local?
faqs.a: A local accountant can meet you face to face, understands your area and is easier to visit when you need to go through paperwork together. It also means you can build a working relationship in person if that suits you.

faqs.q: Is the word "accountant" protected in the UK?
faqs.a: No, on its own it isn't a protected title, so anyone can call themselves an accountant. Protected titles include Chartered Accountant, Chartered Certified Accountant and Chartered Management Accountant, and members are bound by their body's rules.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before I enquire?
faqs.a: It helps to know what kind of business you run, what you need help with and roughly where you're based. You don't need exact figures to start the conversation.

faqs.q: How do I compare quotes from local accountants?
faqs.a: Ask exactly which returns and filings each quote covers, so you're comparing like for like. Quotes are price on application, and it's worth checking what's included before you decide.

extra_heading: What happens when you first meet a local accountant
extra: A first meeting with a local accountant is usually a getting-to-know-you conversation rather than a paperwork drop-off. Expect them to ask what you do, how your business or income is structured, and what you already have in place for records and filings. It's your chance to see whether you'd be comfortable sitting down with this person regularly, which is often the real reason people search for someone local.

Bring what you already have, even if it's incomplete: recent bank statements, any correspondence from HMRC, and notes on how you currently keep records. The accountant can then tell you what they'd need from you and which returns and filings their quote would cover. Ask them to set that out clearly, so you can compare like for like with anyone else you speak to.

It also helps to ask how they prefer to work day to day. Some people want a fixed yearly rhythm of accounts and tax returns, while others want someone to call when a decision comes up, such as taking on an employee or changing how the business is set up. A good accountant should help you plan, not only file, so use the first meeting to judge whether that's how they work.

extra_faqs.q: Should I choose an accountant before or after I start trading?
extra_faqs.a: Many people speak to an accountant before they start, because decisions about how to set up as a sole trader or limited company affect what's involved later. It's also fine to seek one out after you've begun, if you want help catching up with registration and records.

extra_faqs.q: Can a local accountant take over from my current one?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, changing accountant is common, and the new practice usually handles the handover of your records and correspondence with HMRC. Ask at the first meeting what they need from you and from your previous accountant to make the switch smooth.

extra_faqs.q: What if I only need help with one thing, such as a tax return?
extra_faqs.a: That's perfectly reasonable, and it's worth saying so clearly when you enquire. Ask exactly which returns and filings the quote covers, so you know whether it's a one-off piece of work or an ongoing arrangement.
